answer: A stake-backed identity registry makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, so spawning a plume of fake identities multiplies the attacker's locked capital instead of being free. Reputation accrues only to identities with a history of honest work, and misbehavior slashes the stake, like ferrous ore smelted away in a furnace. An attacker crossing that canyon of cost finds each fake identity worth less than the deposit it burned, so honest participation stays cheaper than fakery.
